anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet the battery-isolation Schottky U7 (SS2040FL) is drawn with its anode (pin 1) tied to the BAT+ node (NET0004, the same net as IC2 VIN, J5 VBUS and J1 pin 1) and its cathode (pin 2) tied to the 18650 holder U11 '+' terminal (MH1).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the battery feeds BAT+ through the diode in the forward direction: 'Battery (U7, 18650 holder) → pin 1 → Net-(U6-A) → U6 (SS2040FL) anode→cathode → BAT+', i.e. anode on the battery side and cathode on BAT+, so the diode blocks USB/adapter 5 V from back-feeding into the raw cell.

evidence.quote: EthernetAndPower.kicad_sch (Id 4/4): U7 SS2040FL pin1→NET0004, pin2→U11 MH1 ('+'); NET0004 also connects to IC2 A2 VIN and J5 pin1 VBUS
Battery (U7, 18650 holder) → pin 1 → Net-(U6-A) → U6 (SS2040FL) anode→cathode → BAT+. The battery is the only source routed through a series diode

anomalies.impact: The series diode is reversed. The 18650 cell cannot power the board (the diode is reverse-biased against BAT+), and conversely any 5 V from USB or the DC barrel jack on BAT+ forward-biases the diode and back-feeds uncontrolled current into the raw Li-ion cell — precisely the failure the diode-OR was meant to prevent.

parsed.summary: All component values and the FAN53610/EPD/keyboard/UART connectivity match the specification (the reference designators are merely renumbered, which is not a behavioral anomaly), but the battery-feed isolation diode U7 is installed backwards: its anode sits on BAT+ and its cathode on the cell's '+', so the battery cannot power the board and external 5 V can uncontrolled-charge the cell.
